marks.gloss_en: שנאמר: וישב שלמה על כסא ה'
for מ"ד מלך והדיוט ומלך: Solomon had something else -- he ruled over the upper and lower beings, שנאמר וישב שלמה על כסא ה' (= p_shlomo_elyonim)
one view: Solomon was a king and then a commoner
דכתיב: שפר קדם דריוש והקים על מלכותא לאחשדרפניא מאה ועשרין
והא איכא דריוש, דכתיב דריוש מלכא כתב לכל עממיא ... בכל ארעא -- but there is Darius!
הא איכא שבע דלא מלך עלייהו, דכתיב ... מאה ועשרין -- there are seven he did not rule (= p_shiva_lo_malach)
but there is Darius, as it is written (Dan 6:26): 'Darius the king wrote to all the peoples, nations and tongues who dwell in all the earth: may your peace be great'
ותו ליכא? והא איכא שלמה! -- are there no others? there is Solomon!
לא סליק מלכותיה -- his kingship did not continue (= p_lo_salik_malchut_shlomo). Holds only for מ"ד מלך והדיוט, per 11b.2's הניחא; the schema cannot attach that counter to the answer itself.
the answer: Solomon's kingship did not continue [to the end]
והא הוה סנחריב, דכתיב מי בכל אלהי הארצות -- but there was Sennacherib!
הא איכא ירושלים דלא כבשה -- there is Jerusalem, which he did not conquer (= p_yerushalayim_lo_kavsha)
but there was Sennacherib, as it is written (Isa 36:20): 'who among all the gods of these lands saved their land from my hand?'
והא איכא כורש, דכתיב כל ממלכות הארץ נתן לי ה' -- but there is Cyrus!
התם אשתבוחי הוא דקא משתבח בנפשיה -- there he was praising himself (= p_koresh_mishtabach)
but there is Cyrus, as it is written (Ezra 1:2): 'thus says Cyrus king of Persia: all the kingdoms of the earth the Lord has given me'
מנלן ... דאמר מר: גלו בשבע, גלו בשמונה... -- the tradition cited (no SupportKind names דאמר מר)
as the Master said: they were exiled in the seventh, they were exiled in the eighth, they were exiled in the eighteenth, they were exiled in the nineteenth
דאמר מר: שנה ראשונה כיבש נינוה, שניה כיבש יהויקים -- why the seventh of Jehoiakim's conquest is the eighth of Nebuchadnezzar
וכתיב: ויהי בשלשים ושבע שנה לגלות יהויכין ... בשנת מלכותו -- thirty-seven years of exile at Evil-merodach's accession

'exiled in the seventh' -- of the conquest of Jehoiakim: the exile of Jehoiachin, which is the eighth of Nebuchadnezzar; 'in the eighteenth' -- of the conquest of Jehoiakim: the exile of Zedekiah, the nineteenth of Nebuchadnezzar
תמני ותלתין ושבע -- the eight years before Jehoiachin's exile, plus the thirty-seven
Nebuchadnezzar reigned forty-five years: eight and thirty-seven -- that is forty-five
היינו דקאמר ליה דניאל: ולמאניא די ביתיה היתיו קדמך -- they brought the vessels of His house before you
this is what Daniel said to him: 'you have lifted yourself up against the Lord of heaven, and they brought the vessels of His house before you' (Dan 5:23)
דאיבעי ליה למימני מחרבות ירושלים
Ahasuerus erred in the calculation -- denied by Ahasuerus himself ('I will calculate and not err', 11b.6, 11b.12), asserted by the stam ('he too erred', 11b.13)
בימים ההם כשבת המלך, וכתיב בתריה בשנת שלש למלכו! -- 'when the king sat' against 'in the third year of his reign'
מאי כשבת -- לאחר שנתיישבה דעתו: after his mind was settled (= p_rava_kshevet)

'in those days, when the king Ahasuerus sat [on his throne]' (Esther 1:2) -- the question's '!' presupposes this marks the start of his reign (Steinsaltz spells that out; the Hebrew leaves it implicit)

סוף סוף כמה בצירן? חדיסר. איהו כמה מלך? ארביסר. בארביסר דידיה איבעי ליה למיבני בית המקדש -- counted from Jerusalem's desolations, eleven were lacking and he reigned fourteen, so the Temple should have been built in his fourteenth year; why then is it written 'then the work ceased' (Ezra 4:24)?
שנים מקוטעות הוו -- they were partial years (= p_rava_mekutaot)
why then is it written: 'then the work of the house of God in Jerusalem ceased' (Ezra 4:24)?
as it is written: 'for after seventy years are completed for Babylon I will remember you' (Jer 29:10)
is it written 'for the kingdom of Babylon'? 'for Babylon' is written. What is 'for Babylon'? for the exile of Babylon
